products.name: 300mm Silicon Wafers (Prime Grade)
products.why_imported: No 300mm wafer manufacturing in India; only 150mm pilot lines at MEPL and SITAC.
products.why_it_matters: Wafers are the substrate for every chip; without local supply, India's fab ambitions are built on a single fragile import.
products.can_india_localise: Partial - requires polysilicon + crystal growth capex, 5-7 year horizon.
products.note: Import value reasoned from MNRE-DGCI&S trade triangulation; no India source yet.

products.name: 150mm/200mm Silicon Wafers
products.why_imported: India makes 150mm wafers at pilot scale but capacity is small; cannot meet domestic fab demand.
products.why_it_matters: Legacy-node fabs and discrete devices still need 150/200mm wafers in volume.
products.can_india_localise: Yes - pilots exist; scaling is the next step.
products.note: India has small 150mm capacity at MEPL and SITAC, volume unknown.

products.name: Photoresists (KrF, ArF, EUV)
products.why_imported: Zero domestic photoresist manufacturing; chemistry and purification IP tightly held by JSR, Tokyo Ohka, Shin-Etsu, Fujifilm.
products.why_it_matters: Photoresists are a single point of failure in the lithography stack; a Japan-China trade spat would freeze Indian fabs.
products.can_india_localise: Hard - requires 10+ years of polymer chemistry + GMP-grade purification.
products.note: Strategic inference: import value reasoned from global photoresist TAM share; India-specific data not public.

products.name: EUV Photoresist (Chemically Amplified)
products.why_imported: India has no EUV lithography tools installed; chemically-amplified resists not on any domestic roadmap.
products.why_it_matters: Sub-7nm chip dependency cascades into AI accelerators, defence-grade ASICs and advanced telecom chips.
products.can_india_localise: Hard - depends on EUV scanner access (ASML monopoly) and tin-droplet polymer chemistry.
products.note: Strategic inference; India not on ASML EUV export map.

products.name: EDA Tools (Design Software)
products.why_imported: India has design talent but no commercial EDA toolchain; Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens EDA dominate.
products.why_it_matters: Chip design without indigenous EDA is a strategic liability; export controls on EDA (US 2022 rules) directly constrain Indian AI chip startups.
products.can_india_localise: Hard - 20+ year IP moat; C-DAC has small analog tools but no digital flow.
products.note: Verified: US BIS export controls on EDA documented; market share public.

products.name: Lithography Scanners (DUV & EUV)
products.why_imported: ASML is the sole EUV vendor; Nikon/Canon supply DUV; India has no lithography tool manufacturing.
products.why_it_matters: Lithography is the gating step for any fab; without ASML access, no advanced chip can be made in India.
products.can_india_localise: Hard - requires precision optics, mechatronics and EUV source IP, none of which India has.
products.note: Verified: ASML monopoly public; Tata fab to use ASML DUV tools.

products.name: Dry Etch & Deposition Equipment
products.why_imported: Lam Research, Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron dominate; no Indian OEM.
products.why_it_matters: Etch determines transistor density; an export curb would cripple fabs.
products.can_india_localise: Hard - requires precision mechatronics + plasma physics IP.
products.note: Reasoned estimate based on global fab equipment market shares.

products.name: Leadframes & IC Substrates
products.why_imported: India has small leadframe capacity at Raj Solar / Sahas; IC substrate demand rising with OSAT build-out.
products.why_it_matters: OSAT roadmap (CG Power, Kaynes, Tata) needs substrates; without local supply, value capture stays low.
products.can_india_localise: Yes - leadframes are achievable in 2-3 years; IC substrates harder.
products.note: Reasoned from PLI applicant filings.

sectors.name: Semiconductors
sectors.narrative: India's semiconductor programme is the single largest localisation bet of the decade, anchored by the India Semiconductor Mission and four fab + packaging approvals. Despite this, the country remains 100% import-dependent on logic and memory chips, with the first domestic 28nm node not expected before 2027. The dependency tier is Critical across the board.

sectors.name: Electronics & Consumer Electronics
sectors.narrative: India's electronics manufacturing has tripled in output since 2016 driven by mobile phone PLI, but the bill of materials remains 70-85% imported. PCBs, displays, memory, passives and connectors form the deep dependency layer; the next decade of value capture hinges on substrate-level localisation.

sectors.name: Defence & Strategic Systems
sectors.narrative: Defence imports have fallen from ~70% of capital procurement in 2014-15 to under 40% in 2024-25 by value, but critical sub-systems - aero-engines, sensors, precision munitions, night-vision tubes - remain import-bound. The Positive Indigenisation Lists and Make-I/II projects are the principal de-risking instruments.

sectors.name: Aerospace & Aviation
sectors.narrative: Civil aviation MRO spending by Indian carriers exceeds USD 2 bn annually, of which over 90% leaks offshore. Aerospace-grade alloys, composites, engine modules and avionics line-replaceable units form the dependency spine. HAL, ISRO and private tier-1s anchor the build-out, but tier-2/3 depth is shallow.

sectors.name: Automotive & EV
sectors.narrative: India is the world's largest two-wheeler market and third-largest car market, yet the EV transition has surfaced a fresh dependency stack: lithium cells, cathode active materials, permanent magnets, power modules and BMS ASICs. ACC battery PLI and FAME-II are the lead instruments; cell-level localisation is the binding constraint.

sectors.name: Energy & Renewables
sectors.narrative: Solar PV module manufacturing has scaled under PLI, but wafer and polysilicon capacity is still being built - 100% of wafers were imported in 2024. Wind sector imports high-grade bearings and rare-earth magnets. Electrolyser and green-hydrogen value chains are at infant stage with PLI support.

sectors.name: Medical Devices
sectors.narrative: India imports ~75% of its medical devices by value, concentrated in high-end imaging (CT, MRI), implantables (stents, ortho, cardiac) and IVD reagents. PLI for medical devices supports 18 categories but the bulk of high-value categories still depend on imports from the US, EU and China.

sectors.name: Telecom & Networking
sectors.narrative: Telecom equipment PLI and the mandatory BIS certification regime have helped build domestic BTS and router capacity, but RF front-end chips, optical fibres preforms, and baseband ASICs remain imports. The 5G and 6G stack is the next frontier, with Indigenous 5G (TCS-Jio) as the proof-point.

sectors.name: Capital Goods & Industrial Machinery
sectors.narrative: CNC machine tools, industrial robotics, hydraulic systems and high-pressure pumps form the import base. India's machine tool industry meets ~30% of demand domestically; the rest is imported from Japan, Germany, China and South Korea. Industry 4.0 adoption is widening the tech gap.

sectors.name: Specialty Chemicals & Performance Materials
sectors.narrative: India is a net exporter of bulk agrochemicals and dyes, but remains import-dependent on photoresists, electronic-grade acids, battery electrolytes, high-purity solvents and several catalysts. The China+1 thesis has accelerated specialty capacity additions in Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh.

sectors.name: Pharmaceuticals & APIs
sectors.narrative: India is the pharmacy of the world for formulations but imports ~70% of APIs and KSMs from China, including for antibiotics, paracetamol and cardiovascular drugs. PLI for APIs and Bulk Drug Parks are the de-risking instruments; results visible only from FY26.

sectors.name: Metals & Advanced Materials
sectors.narrative: India is structurally short on specialty steel grades, titanium sponge, rare earths processed intermediates, lithium, cobalt and graphite - the critical-minerals spine for energy transition. Khanij Bidesh India (KABIL) and Critical Minerals Mission are the strategic instruments; downstream processing capacity is the gap.

policies.name: India Semiconductor Mission
policies.summary: USD 10 bn programme to fund fabs, OSAT, compound semiconductors and display manufacturing in India.

policies.name: Semiconductor Ecosystem Policy
policies.summary: Sets fiscal, regulatory and R&D framework for semiconductor and display manufacturing.

policies.name: National Policy on Electronics 2019 (NPE 2019)
policies.summary: Targets USD 400 bn electronics manufacturing by 2025 with a focus on export-led growth.

policies.name: Defence Acquisition Procedure 2020
policies.summary: Codifies Make-I, Make-II, IDDM and strategic partnership models for indigenous procurement.

policies.name: Positive Indigenisation Lists (1-5)
policies.summary: Five lists progressively banning import of ~5000 defence items to drive domestic procurement.

policies.name: Make-I & Make-II Procedure
policies.summary: Government funds up to 70% (Make-I) or 100% (Make-II) of prototype development by Indian industry.

policies.name: National Civil Aeronautics Policy 2016 (review 2024)
policies.summary: Framework for MRO, regional connectivity, aerospace manufacturing; review underway for component PLI.

policies.name: Aerospace & Defence Make-in-India (A&D)
policies.summary: Cross-ministry initiative to attract FDI and build tier-2/3 aerospace supply chains.

policies.name: FAME India Scheme Phase II
policies.summary: INR 11500 cr scheme for EV demand stimulus; succeeded by PM E-Drive in 2024.

policies.name: PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-Drive)
policies.summary: INR 10900 cr scheme supporting 2.5M EVs and 88k public charging points over two years.

policies.name: PM Pollution Clean (PLDPC) - component localisation
policies.summary: Phased localisation of EV components including BMS, motors and drivetrains.

policies.name: National Green Hydrogen Mission
policies.summary: INR 19744 cr outlay to make India a green-hydrogen hub; includes electrolyser manufacturing PLI.

policies.name: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
policies.summary: INR 75000 cr central subsidy to install rooftop solar on 10M households by 2026.

policies.name: National Medical Device Policy 2023
policies.summary: Sets regulatory, infrastructure, R&D and skill roadmap to grow medical devices to USD 50 bn by 2030.

policies.name: Medical Device Rules 2017 (CDSCO)
policies.summary: Risk-based regulatory regime for medical devices, expanded in 2020 to cover all device classes.

policies.name: Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF)
policies.summary: USD 70M annual grant for Indian R&D in 5G/6G, quantum and AI-native telecom.

policies.name: 5G India Rollout & Indigenous Stack
policies.summary: Indigenous 5G core & RAN (TCS-Jio) deployed across all 28 states; 6G testbed in IIT-Madras.

policies.name: National Capital Goods Policy
policies.summary: Targets tripling of domestic capital-goods output to INR 7.5L cr; review due 2025.

policies.name: Scheme for Enhancement of Competitiveness in Capital Goods
policies.summary: Centres of Excellence, Industry 4.0 adoption, skilling in CNC, robotics and additive.

policies.name: National Chemical & Petrochemical Policy
policies.summary: Sets vision for USD 304 bn chemicals industry by 2030 with PCPIR clusters.

policies.name: Scheme for Bulk Drug Parks
policies.summary: INR 3000 cr grant for three bulk drug parks (HP, AP, Telangana) with common facilities.

policies.name: Pharma Policy 2024 (draft)
policies.summary: Strengthens API self-reliance, regulatory capacity and clinical research ecosystem.

policies.name: Critical Minerals Mission
policies.summary: USD 500M mission for domestic exploration, overseas acquisition and processing of 24 critical minerals.

policies.name: KABIL Argentina Lithium MoU
policies.summary: KABIL to acquire and develop lithium brine blocks in Catamarca, Argentina.

policies.name: Mines & Minerals (Development & Regulation) Amendment Act 2023
policies.summary: Adds 24 critical minerals, allows private exploration, introduces auction of mining blocks.

policies.name: PLI Umbrella Framework
policies.summary: INR 1.97L cr umbrella covering 14 sectoral PLIs; 740 applications approved, INR 1.4L cr investment projected.

policies.name: Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan
policies.summary: Five-pillar self-reliance agenda including MSME support, FDI liberalisation and PLI schemes.

policies.name: Make in India
policies.summary: National initiative to raise manufacturing share of GDP to 25% and attract FDI across 25 sectors.

policies.name: Industrial Policy Resolution (DPIIT 2024 review)
policies.summary: Revises industrial policy to align with PLI, FTAs and Industry 4.0; draft circulated 2024.

policies.name: India-UK FTA (signed 2025)
policies.summary: Reduces tariffs on ~99% of trade; opens UK government procurement for Indian firms.
